title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Dated 11.1.84 and headed 'Chirurgie conforme', section (4). Grothendieck sets up the foundations for cutting and gluing Riemann surfaces.

Definition. A conformal surface with boundary is a surface with an atlas of local charts. Near a boundary point the charts are modelled on the closed upper half-plane H̄ = {Im z ≥ 0} ⊂ ℂ.

Sheaf description. In the oriented case (equivalently, a holomorphic structure) the structure can be given by a sheaf of ℂ-algebras. On the model H̄, its stalk at a point x ∈ ∂H = ℝ consists of germs of functions that extend holomorphically to a neighbourhood of x in ℂ.

Warning. This sheaf is not to be confused with the larger subsheaf of the sheaf of continuous complex functions made of continuous functions that are holomorphic in Int(X).

Theorem 1. The conformal structure of a bordered conformal surface X is determined by its restriction to Int(X). That restriction already determines the sheaf of continuous functions that are conformal in the interior.

Proof strategy, continued on the next page.
- One must recover the boundary charts. They should be exactly the topological open embeddings U → H̄, sending boundary to boundary, that are holomorphic in the interior.
- This reduces to Lemma 1: an open embedding f : U ↪ H̄ (U open in H̄) that is holomorphic on U∩H extends holomorphically across U∩ℝ.
- The lemma is a case of the Schwarz reflection principle, since f is real on U∩ℝ.
- Finally one checks that the extended germ is invertible (nonzero derivative), so f is a genuine holomorphic chart.

Purpose. These are preliminaries for 'conformal surgery': gluing bordered Riemann surfaces along boundary circles. The previous page develops the gluing data in that language: oriented 'toric circles' (U-torsors), complex lines with a gauge, and the identification Isom(C'^-, C'') ≃ dualities between complex lines. That is the bookkeeping for sewing along boundary components.
errors: No mathematical error. Theorem 1 is a uniqueness statement: given the topological surface with boundary, there is at most one bordered conformal structure extending the interior one. Existence of an extension is not claimed and indeed fails in general. The text does not spell this out, but the wording 'est connue quand' is consistent with uniqueness only.
Minor gap, filled on the next page: invertibility of the extended germ follows from injectivity (an injective holomorphic germ has nonzero derivative). Grothendieck only sketches this.

ideas.what: Bordered Riemann surfaces defined by charts modelled on the closed upper half-plane, and equivalently by a sheaf of ℂ-algebras of germs extending holomorphically across the boundary
ideas.modern_name: bordered Riemann surface (Ahlfors–Sario); structure sheaf of a bordered Riemann surface

ideas.what: Conformal structure on a bordered surface is determined by the interior structure, via Schwarz reflection
ideas.modern_name: uniqueness of boundary extension of conformal structure / Schwarz reflection principle

ideas.what: Programme of 'conformal surgery': gluing bordered Riemann surfaces along boundary circles, with gluing data encoded by U-torsors and dualities of complex lines (previous page)
ideas.modern_name: sewing of Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundaries (Segal's CFT axioms, Vafa, Huang)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Jan 1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower and surfaces with boundary components and gluing, but not this analytic set-up in detail

missed.claim: The page is part of a Jan 1984 manuscript on surgery (sewing) of conformal surfaces with boundary. Read together with the neighbouring pages on gluing data along boundary circles, it predates Segal's sewing formalism for conformal field theory by several years. This page itself contains only routine foundations.
missed.quote: Chirurgie conforme (4) Surfaces conformes à bord.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is of historical interest as an independent early development of the sewing category of Riemann surfaces, linked to the Teichmüller tower of the Esquisse. Mathematically, this page adds nothing new.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is standard foundational material: definition of bordered Riemann surfaces and uniqueness of boundary structure via Schwarz reflection. Only the surrounding project (conformal surgery, contemporaneous with the Esquisse) is of mild historical interest.
transcription_corrections: 'À un peu confondre avec le sous-faisceau' should read 'À ne pas confondre avec le sous-faisceau'.
'sous-faisceau plus grand des faisceaux des fonctions complexes continues' — read 'du faisceau des fonctions complexes continues'.
'qui sont hol dans Int(X)': the manuscript has 'qui sont hol. dans Int(X)'.
'Il suffit de voir que cela permet de reconstituer' — the leading 'Il' is written over a correction; the reading is fine.
